claims.limits: Not Campus-specific. Enrollment at some point and a mixed shelter/housing classification do not establish retention, permanent housing or an effective grievance/accommodation remedy.

claims.claim: Actual Campus notice delivery, accessible grievance/accommodation operation, corrective directives, implemented readmission, sustained retention and successful transitions remain unverified in this pass.
claims.limits: No named-resident investigation, private record, legal event analysis or Campus-specific performance audit was undertaken.

counterevidence_and_ordinary_explanation.text: Later City reports and the accessible report index demonstrate reporting activity after the audit. This constrains any claim that the historical Not Started labels prove continuing inactivity. Audit closure/verification and management publication can occur on different schedules.

City-reported noncongregate transitions are positive evidence at a pooled-program level. They cannot be reassigned to Campus, and differing participants, program designs or observation periods could affect comparisons.

Shelter enrollment may be useful progress even when permanent housing is unavailable. A short or repeated stay does not by itself show failed protection; retained access and later destination were not measured here.

Public records may omit operational documents, deidentified results or privately handled remedies. Search/extraction misses and the operator PDF size failure do not establish absence of compliant practice.
